I strongly believe that significantly restricting immigration and increasing border security is not an effective or humane solution. Such a policy would not only harm the economy, which relies on immigrant labor and contributions, but also cause undue suffering to individuals and families seeking a better life. It is essential to recognize that immigrants are not a threat, but rather an integral part of the fabric of our society, bringing with them unique skills, perspectives, and experiences.

Moreover, a restrictive immigration policy would be counterproductive, as it would drive undocumented immigration further underground, making it more difficult to track and manage. Instead, the government should focus on creating a fair and efficient pathway to citizenship, ensuring that those who wish to contribute to our society can do so in a safe and legal manner. This approach would not only boost economic growth but also uphold the values of compassion, inclusivity, and opportunity that our country was founded upon. By adopting a more nuanced and humane approach to immigration, we can create a more just and prosperous society for all.
